findings.description: The database username and password are interpolated into EC2 user data and written to a local PHP configuration file. EC2 user data is retrievable by principals with instance-describe access and may also persist in Terraform state, broadening exposure of the database credential.

The RDS instance is explicitly configured with publicly_accessible = true, giving it a public network endpoint. Although the shown security group ingress is VPC-scoped, this unnecessarily exposes the database to internet-reachable attack paths if security-group rules change or other network controls are bypassed.
storage_encrypted = false leaves RDS database storage, backups, snapshots, and automated backups unencrypted at rest, exposing database contents if underlying storage artifacts are accessed.

This rule permits all protocols and ports from the database security group to 0.0.0.0/0. It provides an unrestricted outbound path for data exfiltration or command-and-control traffic from a compromised database environment.

The EC2 application role grants all S3, EC2, and RDS actions against every resource. A compromise of the instance or its metadata credentials would permit broad account-wide resource access and likely privilege escalation paths.

MySQL port 3306 is open to the entire VPC CIDR rather than only the application security group or required hosts. Any compromised or unauthorized workload in the VPC can attempt to connect to the database.
